speaker: Doctor
text: I see you have blisters on your forearm and ulcers on your mucosal surfaces; can you tell me how long these symptoms have been present and if they appear in crops?

speaker: Patient
text: 50-year-old female. The patient reports the appearance of blisters on her forearm 3 days ago, accompanied by pain in her left cheek when eating and pain during sexual intercourse for the past week. She has been hiking in the woods recently but denies contact with poison ivy. She has a history of hypertension and osteoarthritis, recently started taking captopril, and discontinued meloxicam 2 weeks ago. Family history includes pernicious anemia and Graves' disease.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your recent start on captopril and the combination of painful skin blisters and oral ulcers, I need to confirm if the blisters have burst to form erosions and if you have any fever or joint pain. REQUEST TEST: Complete blood count (CBC) with differential and erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR). REQUEST TEST: C3 and C4 complement levels. DIAGNOSIS READY: Drug-induced cutaneous vasculitis secondary to captopril use.
